issues.body:
`scan_text()` calls `truncation_offence()` independently for each physical line, while `_NAME_RE` only recognizes the line containing `name:` or `run-name:`. A valid YAML plain scalar may continue on a more-indented following line, for example `- name: Publish cadence
          for issue #1135`; YAML treats the whitespace-prefixed `#1135` as a comment, but the continuation line does not match `_NAME_RE`, so the gate reports no offence. This contradicts the stated rule that every affected plain-scalar mapping entry is flagged and leaves a silent false-negative in a gating check.
issues.fix_hint: Track indentation and plain-scalar continuation lines after an unquoted `name:`/`run-name:` entry until the mapping value ends, checking those continuation lines for the comment trigger. Add a self-test containing a multiline plain scalar with ` #1234` on a continuation line, plus a safe multiline case, and verify the reported intended/truncated values.
issues.title: Multiline plain-scalar names bypass the truncation gate

verdict.summary: The remediation quotes the currently known truncated workflow names, and both the bundled self-test and live scan pass. However, the lexical gate does not cover multiline plain scalars even though its documented rule promises to flag every unquoted `name:`/`run-name:` plain scalar containing a whitespace-prefixed `#`. YAML permits a plain scalar to continue on subsequent indented lines, where the issue reference can be silently consumed as a comment; the scanner examines only the mapping's first line and therefore passes that defect. Add continuation-aware scanning and a regression fixture before making this gating.
